text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia outlines government's plan to speed up privatisation of state-owned firms through mass sell-off, allocating free shares for workers and young people. Ouyahia, speaking at a news conference, urges people to have a realistic view of the difficult context in which Algeria is reforming its economy and building a multi-party democracy.
- Seven people, including young shepherds, were killed by gunmen in Moulay el Arbi small town in the southwestern province of Saida.

- Ouyahia, behaving like a politician sensing his career is threatened by public discontent, strives to defend his government's performance. People, who will vote in June 5 to elect parliament, remember well that Ouyahia had tried to cut salaries to pay due wages for workers in the building sector.
- Ouyahia kicks off his personal campaign promising voters there will no tax increase in 1998. Ouyahia stands as candidate for the 380-seat National Assembly.

- French court due to rule on Tuesday on lawsuit by British Airways seeking greater security at Charles de Gaulle airport after the French authorities allowed Air Algerie to resume flights to Paris. The Algerian airline resumed flights on Friday after it stopped services to Paris two years ago in protest at being forced to use a remote terminal after Moslem rebels hickjacked a French plane in Algiers and forced it to fly to France.
- Algeria awaits the arrival of 200 foreign observers to monitor the June 5 parliamentary elections.
- Prime Minister Ouyahia says Algeria will not seek a third foreign debt rescheduling.
- Secular opposition Socialist Forces Front fields 34 candiate lists across the country.
